source_text: Plerosque tamen hoc opus, ut publicationem sui, aut suffugere aut de die in diem differre. Praesumo, pudoris magis memores quam salutis; velut illi qui in partibus verecundioribus corporis contracta vexatione conscientiam medentium vitant et ita cum erubescentia sua pereunt. Intolerandum scilicet pudori domino offenso satisfacere, saluti prodactae reformari. Nae tu verecundia bonus, ad delinquendum expandens frontem, ad deprecandum vero subducens. Ego rubori locum non facio, cum plus de detrimento eius acquiro, cum ipse hominem quodammodo exhortatur, Ne me respexeris, dicens, per te mihi melius est perire. Certe periculum eius tunc, si forte, onerosum est, cum penes insultaturos in risiloquio consistit, ubi de alterius ruina alter attollitur, ubi prostrato superscenditur: ceterum inter fratres atque conservos, ubi communis spes, metus, gaudium, dolor, passio, quia communis spiritus de communi domino et patre, quid tu hos aliud quam te opinaris? Quid consortes casuum tuorum ut plausores fugis? Non potest corpus de unius membri vexatione laetum agere; condoleat universum et ad remedium conlaboret necesse est. In uno et altero ecclesia est, ecclesia vero Christus. Ergo cum te ad fratrum genua protendis, Christum contrectas, Christum exoras. Aeque illi cum super te lacrimas agunt, Christus patitur, Christus patrem deprecatur. Facile impetratur semper quod filius postulat. Grande plane emolumentum verecundiae occultatio delicti pollicetur. Videlicet si quid humanae notitiae subduxerimus, proinde et deum celabimus? Adeone existimatio hominum et dei conscientia comparantur? An melius est damnatum latere quam palam absolvi? Miserum est sic ad exomologesin pervenire! Malo enim ad miseriam pervenitur; sed ubi paenitendum est, desinit miserum, quia factum est salutare. Miserum est secari et cauterio exuri et pulveris alicuius mordacitate anxiari; tamen quae per insuavitatem medentur, et emolumento curationis offensam sui excusant et praesentem iniuriam superventurae utilitatis gratia commendant.
thought_title: Shame must not delay public confession
orientation: Tertullian is addressing Christians who shrink from public confession because of embarrassment, and he argues that shame before fellow believers is misplaced.
pass_a_gloss: Yet most people either avoid this work, as a public exposure of themselves, or put it off from day to day. I presume, they are more mindful of shame than of salvation; like those who, when a disease has been contracted in the more private parts of the body, avoid the notice of physicians and so perish along with their embarrassment. It is intolerable, of course, to make amends to an offended Lord for the sake of shame, to be restored to a salvation that has been brought forth. Truly you are good in modesty, stretching out your forehead for sinning, but withdrawing it for begging. I give no place to blushing, since I gain more from its loss, since it in a way urges the man himself, saying, Do not look back at me, it is better for me to perish through you. Certainly its danger is burdensome then, if ever, when it consists among those who will mock in derisive talk, where one person is lifted up by another's ruin, where one climbs over the one laid low: but among brothers and fellow servants, where there is common hope, fear, joy, grief, suffering, because there is a common spirit from a common Lord and father, what do you think these people are other than yourself? Why do you flee the sharers of your misfortunes as if they were applauders? The body cannot act joyfully about the affliction of one member; the whole must suffer with it and labor together for the remedy. In one and another the church is, and the church is Christ. Therefore when you stretch yourself out at the knees of the brothers, you touch Christ, you entreat Christ. Likewise when they shed tears over you, Christ suffers, Christ entreats the Father. What the Son asks is always easily obtained. Great indeed is the advantage that the concealment of sin promises to shame. Of course, if we have withdrawn something from human knowledge, shall we likewise hide it from God? Are the estimation of humans and the knowledge of God compared on equal terms? Or is it better to lie hidden as a condemned person than to be openly absolved? It is wretched to arrive at public confession in this way! For one arrives at wretchedness by evil; but where there is need to repent, it ceases to be wretched, because it has become salutary. It is wretched to be cut and burned with a cautery and tormented by the biting of some powder; yet the things that heal through unpleasantness both excuse the offense done to oneself by the benefit of the cure and commend the present injury for the sake of the usefulness that will follow.

choices.why: Keeps the reflexive force of sui and the sense of making oneself public, matching the shame context.

choices.english: more mindful of shame than of salvation
choices.why: Preserves the comparative structure and the contrast between shame and salvation, both key terms in the argument.

choices.english: to be restored to a salvation that has been brought forth
choices.why: prodactae is taken as 'brought forth, produced'; the rendering keeps the passive infinitive and the dative of salus.
rejected: to be reformed for a prolonged salvation

choices.term: ad delinquendum expandens frontem, ad deprecandum vero subducens
choices.english: stretching out your forehead for sinning, but withdrawing it for begging
choices.why: Keeps the parallel gerund constructions and the body metaphor of the forehead, which is central to the shame argument.
rejected: shameless in sinning but shy in praying

choices.term: In uno et altero ecclesia est, ecclesia vero Christus
choices.english: In one and another the church is, and the church is Christ
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the theological identification of the gathered believers with Christ, which grounds the following argument.
rejected: Where two or three are gathered, there is the church, and the church is Christ

choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'sin' for delictum and keeps the abstract noun occultatio.

pass_b_english: Yet many people either avoid this work as a public exposure of themselves or put it off from day to day. I presume they are more mindful of shame than of salvation, like those who, when disease has settled in the more private parts of the body, avoid the doctors' knowledge and so perish along with their embarrassment. It is intolerable, apparently, for shame to make amends to an offended Lord, to be restored to a salvation that has been put at risk. A fine thing your modesty is: boldly showing your face for sinning, but hiding it for begging. I make no room for blushing, since I gain more from its loss, since shame in some way urges the person on, saying, 'Do not look at me; it is better for me to perish through you.' Certainly its danger is burdensome, if at all, when it stands among those who will mock with derisive talk, where one person is lifted up by another's ruin, where someone climbs over the one who has fallen. But among brothers and fellow servants, where there is common hope, fear, joy, sorrow, suffering—because there is a common Spirit from a common Lord and Father—why do you think of them as anything other than yourself? Why do you flee those who share your misfortunes as if they were applauders? The body cannot rejoice over the affliction of one member; the whole must grieve with it and labor together for the remedy. In one and another the church is, and the church is Christ. So when you stretch yourself out at the brothers' knees, you touch Christ, you beg Christ. Likewise when they shed tears over you, Christ suffers, Christ pleads with the Father. What the Son asks is always easily obtained. The concealment of sin promises a great advantage to modesty, to be sure. If we have withdrawn something from human knowledge, will we hide it from God just the same? Are human opinion and God's knowledge really comparable? Is it better to be damned in hiding than to be absolved openly? It is a wretched thing to come to public confession this way! Yes, one comes to wretchedness—but where repentance is required, it ceases to be wretched, because it has become salutary. It is wretched to be cut and burned with a cautery and tormented by the bite of some powder; yet the things that heal through unpleasantness excuse their offense by the benefit of the cure and commend their present injury for the sake of the usefulness to come.

problems.quote: to be restored to a salvation that has been brought forth
problems.why: 'prodactae' = 'endangered/jeopardized', not 'brought forth'. The sense is restoring a salvation at risk.
problems.fix: to be restored to a salvation that has been put at risk
problems.ruling: Latin "saluti prodactae" = ‘to the salvation that has been exposed/jeopardized’, not ‘brought forth’.

edits.old: to be restored to a salvation that has been brought forth
edits.new: to be restored to a salvation that has been put at risk

fixed: Corrected 'prodactae' from 'brought forth' to 'put at risk' (source: 'saluti prodactae reformari').

problems.why: Intro uses both 'public confession' and 'discipline of confession and humiliation' for the same rite, possibly confusing readers.
problems.fix: Use 'public confession' consistently; note the Greek term once.

variants.text: a discipline of confession and humiliation

problems.quote: since it in some way urges the person on, saying, 'Do not look at me; it is better for me to perish through you.'
problems.why: The 'it' that speaks is shame/modesty personified, but the referent is unclear; reader may think a person is speaking.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'since shame in some way urges the person on, saying…'

problems.quote: stretching out your forehead for sinning, but withdrawing it for begging
problems.why: 'Stretching out your forehead' is a puzzling literal rendering; likely means 'boldly facing' or 'pushing forward' for sin.
problems.fix: Render as 'boldly showing your face for sinning, but hiding it for begging.'

fixed: Glossary problem: no edit needed; the brief's glossary already specifies 'public confession' as the English for exomologesis, and the English uses it consistently.
Speaker problem: the source 'cum ipse hominem quodammodo exhortatur' refers to shame (pudor) personified, so clarifying 'shame' is warranted.
Mistranslation: 'expandens frontem' means boldly showing one's face, so the suggested rendering is more accurate.

last_rejected.quote: A fine thing your modesty is
last_rejected.why: 'bonus' is masculine adjective, not noun 'a fine thing'; Tertullian addresses the person as 'good sir'.
last_rejected.fix: You are a fine fellow in your modesty
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'verecundia' (modesty) linked with 'bonus' yields 'modesty is good'; translation conveys same sense despite phrasing

last_rejected.quote: It is intolerable, apparently, for shame to make amends to an offended Lord, to be restored to a salvation that has been put at risk.
last_rejected.source_quote: Intolerandum scilicet pudori domino offenso satisfacere, saluti prodactae reformari.
last_rejected.why: Latin says shame should *satisfy* the offended Lord, not *make amends*; the English adds a false sense of atonement.
last_rejected.fix: It is intolerable, indeed, that shame should satisfy the offended Lord, that salvation which has been jeopardized be restored.
last_rejected.ruling: "satisfacere" means to make amends or satisfy; rendering as "make amends" is within normal range, not a meaning change.
